blogs.title: From Predictor to Prep Cook: How LLMs Are Reinventing Spreadsheet Analysis
blogs.description: Explores the core paradigm shift introduced by FeatLLM, where instead of asking an LLM to directly predict every row in a spreadsheet, we use it as an expert 'feature engineer.' The post will break down how generating logical rules upfront and leaving the final math to a simple, lightweight model unlocks the true potential of AI for tabular data.

blogs.title: The High Cost of AI Predictions: Why FeatLLM Skips the LLM at Inference Time
blogs.description: Dives into the operational bottlenecks of current AI tabular models—namely, the astronomical cost and latency of sending every single data row through an LLM API. This post explains how FeatLLM's architecture solves this by only querying the LLM during the training/prep phase, resulting in lightning-fast, budget-friendly predictions.

blogs.title: Doing More with Less: How AI is Solving the Data Scarcity Problem in Healthcare and Finance
blogs.description: Focuses on the 'few-shot learning' capability of FeatLLM. We'll discuss how industries like healthcare and finance often struggle with limited labeled data. The post will explain how FeatLLM leverages an LLM's 'prior knowledge' to achieve top-tier performance with only 4 data samples, matching traditional models that require 32.

blogs.title: Taming Massive Spreadsheets: How Ensemble Bagging Solves the LLM Context Limit
blogs.description: A deep dive into the technical mechanics of how FeatLLM handles wide and complex tabular datasets. The post will explain how the framework uses 'feature bagging' and ensemble methods to bypass the prompt size limitations of LLMs, allowing it to process datasets with over 100 columns without breaking a sweat.

blogs.title: Filtering the Noise: How AI Feature Engineering Stays Resilient Against Bad Data
blogs.description: Explores FeatLLM's resilience against 'spurious correlations'—the irrelevant or noisy columns that often confuse traditional machine learning models in low-data scenarios. This post will detail how FeatLLM forces the LLM to use common sense and domain knowledge to extract rules, successfully ignoring junk data.
